processing: A special green tea made from downy young shoots. The exact steps are not widely published.
harvest_season: Spring; as with other fine Hunan greens, the earliest tender pickings are the prized ones.
appearance_dry: Shoots densely covered in silvery down, which gives the tea its silver-peak name.
appearance_liquor: Pale and clear, as is typical of downy Hunan spring greens, often slightly hazy from the down.
appearance_wet: Tender, even shoots, as is usual for a tea of this grade.
taste_profile: Little tasting detail is recorded; expect the fresh, delicate sweetness typical of a downy pan-fired spring green.

brewing.notes: General settings for a downy green. Haze from the down is normal, and cooler water keeps the shoots from going flat.

vintage_note: As with other Chinese famous greens, it is usually sold as the current spring harvest, ideally drunk within the year. It is not a tea to age.
description:
Gaoqiao Yinfeng, Gaoqiao Silver Peak, is a Changsha green tea named by Hunan's own provincial overview among its well-known teas. The name means silver peak, and it is generally described as a modern tea from the provincial tea research institute at Gaoqiao.

The making steps are not widely published, so do not assume a particular style from the name alone.

Firm tasting notes are hard to come by, so expect what is typical of downy Hunan spring greens: delicate and lightly sweet. A cloudy cup in a downy green is usually just down in suspension.

When buying, ask for the harvest year and look for abundant, pale down.
history: The tea is generally dated to the late 1950s and credited to the Hunan Provincial Tea Research Institute at Gaoqiao, though the exact year is given differently. Guo Moruo is said to have tasted it in 1964 and written a poem about it, which helped its reputation. Later awards are not reliably documented here.
